issue.title: ACP parallel tool calls lose their arguments except the last one.

steps:
Please set up this small Python package in the current directory. Create all four files exactly as given, then run `python3 main.py` and tell me exactly what it printed.

shapes/__init__.py:
```python
from .circle import area as circle_area
from .square import area as square_area
```

shapes/circle.py:
```python
import math

def area(r):
    return round(math.pi * r * r, 2)
```

shapes/square.py:
```python
def area(side):
    return side * side
```

main.py:
```python
from shapes import circle_area, square_area

print("circle:", circle_area(2))
print("square:", square_area(3))
```
expected: Each parallel tool call should receive its own streamed arguments.
defect: ACP parallel tool calls lose their arguments except the last one.

fault location.explanation: The buffer and destination tool are not selected by call id.

Root cause: Source at the tested commit uses one shared JSON buffer, clears it on each start, and assigns each end event to tool_calls.back(). OpenAI Chat closes calls together, so earlier calls remain empty. Ten frozen H2 trials are retained and archived analysis reports argument loss in all ten. Successful later retries do not negate the intermediate tool error. sandbox off was used because the container could not run claybin. No fresh runtime reproduction was performed during this organization. Exact first fixing commit has not been established. Root steps describe the selected original case; other run-local cases can differ. Retained observations are not automatically independent same-prompt trials.
